div.head: Wer 6.1
div.ab: Siððan man mot mid lufe ofgan, gif man hwilefulle freondrædne habban.
Syððan man mot mid lufe ofgan, gif man wille fulle freondræddene habban.
Deinde liceat per amorem procedere, si perfectam uelit amicorum consocietatem habere.
Nachher mag man [der Totschläger], wenn man volle Freundschaft [von der beleidigten Sippe] erhalten will, [das] erlangen durch private Versöhnung.
Afterwards one [the slayer], if one wishes to have full friendship [with the injured kin], may obtain [it] by private reconciliation.
Afterwards, one may depart with love, if one wish to have full friendship.
div.note: U: translator probably Wormald, The Making of English Law (named in the original spreadsheet’s sub-header rows): check; H reads ‘hwile’, to be corrected to ‘wille’. B has a paragraph break after this clause.

note.seg: Not ‘depart, advance’ or ‘bring to an end (Steenstrup Danelag 304)’
